Solving a Sum End to End — One Flow · Maths, EEE, Basic Engineering & Aptitude Trees

Same 9 steps for every sum. Steps 1–4 take under a minute and decide everything else. Step 2 uses the trees (D Maths, E EEE, F Basic engineering, G Aptitude — every past question has a branch, see H): start at the top box, follow the branch whose signal words appear in the question, and the leaf gives you the first formula and what to do next.

A · One flow for every sum

1 · READ THE LAST LINE

Write the TARGET as a symbol with its unit: “find t” → t = ? (s). Note MCQ / MSQ / NAT and marks.

▼

2 · CLASSIFY

Maths or EEE? → subject → topic, using the signal words (Maths tree / EEE tree below). This tells you which formula family to open.

▼

3 · LIST THE GIVENS

Symbol = value with unit. Convert at once: kV→V, MVA→VA, µF→F, mH→H, rpm→rad/s (×2π/60), % → decimal, 50 Hz → ω = 314.16 rad/s.

▼

4 · DRAW THE MODEL

10-second sketch: circuit / phasor / equivalent circuit / block diagram / per-phase diagram / matrix. Mark knowns in ink and the target with “?”.

▼

5 · LINK (gap tree)

Pick the formula that CONTAINS the target. Any unknown in it? → find a second formula for that unknown → repeat until every leaf is a given. (Example below.)

▼

6 · LOOK FOR A SHORTCUT

Special case (ζ = 1, s = 0, balanced load, triangular matrix), standard result, symmetry, or work backwards from the options.

▼

7 · RUN

Compute from the leaves up the gap tree. Keep 4 significant figures until the last step.

▼

8 · CHECK (10 s)

Unit right? Sign right? Range sane (η < 1, pf ≤ 1, 0 < s < 1, probability 0–1)? Matches an option? NAT: correct decimals.

▼

9 · DECIDE

Over 1.5× the time for its marks (1 mark ≈ 2 min, 2 marks ≈ 4 min) with no progress → mark, move on, come back in the next pass.

1. READ: target P(X = 0).

2. CLASSIFY: “average rate”, rare events → Poisson, λ = 2.

3. LINK: P(X = k) = e−λλᵏ/k!, k = 0.

4. RUN: e−2 = 0.1353.

5. CHECK: between 0 and 1 ✓. Answer 0.135.

EEE · Machines

4-pole, 50 Hz induction motor runs at 1440 rpm; rotor copper loss 240 W. Mechanical power developed?

1. READ: target Pm (W).

2. CLASSIFY: EEE → Machines → Induction motor (“rpm”, “rotor copper loss”).

3. LINK (gap tree): Pm = Pg(1 − s) → Pg = Pcu2/s → s = (Ns − N)/Ns → Ns = 120f/P.

4. RUN (leaves up): Ns = 1500 rpm; s = 0.04; Pg = 240/0.04 = 6000 W; Pm = 6000 × 0.96 = 5760 W.

5. CHECK: Pm < Pg ✓, s between 0 and 1 ✓. Answer 5.76 kW.

EEE · Circuits (find t)

R = 1 kΩ, C = 1 µF, uncharged, connected to 10 V DC at t = 0. When does VC reach 5 V?

1. READ: target t (s).

2. CLASSIFY: EEE → Circuits → Transient, one C → first order.

3. LINK: t = τ ln[(V0 − V∞)/(VC − V∞)]; τ = RC; V0 = 0; V∞ = 10 V.

4. RUN: τ = 1 ms; t = 1 ms × ln(−10/−5) = 1 ms × ln 2 = 0.693 ms.

5. CHECK: half-way in 0.69τ — the standard result ✓. Answer 0.693 ms.
